subject: DeltaStack: request for temporary SLA carve-out for filter-induced tool call timeouts
messages:
From: Rohit Singh <rohit@deltastack.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jacob Low <jacob.low@deltastack.ai>, Emily Ng <emily.ng@deltastack.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary SLA carve-out for filter-related tool-call timeouts

Hi Evelyn —

We're seeing a recurring issue in our production integration where Redwood's content filter is triggering synchronous schema revalidation that causes downstream tool-calls to timeout. The client-facing impact is increased 5xx/timeout errors during peak inference bursts, which in turn is pushing our observed p95 latency above the contracted target.

We have attached a short sample (schema-sample.json) and a trimmed log bundle (deltastack_failure_logs.zip) showing repeated tool-call failures tied to filter hits. Our engineering team is actively testing a non-blocking filter path but needs a short window to validate without being in breach of the SLA.

Request: a limited, time-boxed carve-out for 'filter-induced tool-call latency' for up to two weeks while we validate the mitigation. During the window we'll accept telemetry tagging and stricter alerting from your side.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can agree to a narrow carve-out and any constraints you need (rate limits, telemetry hooks, rollback conditions)? We want to avoid procurement holdups for the renewal.

Thanks,
Rohit Singh
CTO, DeltaStack Analytics
[attachment: deltastack_failure_logs.zip (application/zip)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary SLA carve-out for filter-related tool-call timeouts

Team — FYI, DeltaStack is asking for a short carve-out while they validate a non-blocking filter path. Key asks: 2-week window, telemetry tagging, and that we won't escalate SLA credits immediately if the issue is filter-induced.

Can you: 1) confirm root cause and whether the filter behavior counts as a platform-excluded event, 2) propose exact carve-out language we can present to them, and 3) identify required guardrails (telemetry hooks, rate caps, time-box).

I copied Ben for commercial language. Please treat this as high priority — they're up for renewal and this could block procurement if we don't move fast.

Thanks,
Evelyn

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary SLA carve-out for filter-related tool-call timeouts

Quick root-cause summary: aggressive filter hits are invoking a synchronous tool-call path for structured output verification. When the filter trips, our runtime currently blocks the token stream until the verification completes (we did this historically to avoid emitting disallowed structured outputs). That synchronous path increases tail latency and in high-concurrency workloads can push p95/p99 past SLA targets.

Mitigation options we can deploy quickly:
- Short-term (days): flip to async filter pass-through for flagged prompts with a fallback that strips the flagged field and issues an explanatory tag; requires telemetry and a conservative sampling rate.
- Mid-term (1–2 weeks): onboard a lighter-weight verification variant and a model-variant fallback that avoids the heavy synchronous check.

I recommend we offer a 14-day, monitored carve-out limited to "filter-induced tool-call latency" with these guardrails:
- DeltaStack must enable a telemetry flag so we can tag affected requests (we'll provide a hook).
- Rate cap: carve-out applies only to up to 20% of calls by volume or 500 RPS (whichever lower).
- Auto-revert: if errors or latency exceed thresholds (we'll define), the carve-out is revoked automatically.

I've attached my notes.

—Karthik
[attachment: root_cause_notes.txt (text/plain)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rohit Singh <rohit@deltastack.ai>, Emily Ng <emily.ng@deltastack.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-23T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed SLA amendment language for filter-related carve-out

Hi Rohit / Emily —

Thanks for flagging this. Attached is a short proposed amendment draft that defines a narrow exception:
- Definition: "Filter-induced tool-call latency" describes latency or timeouts directly caused by the operation of Redwood's content-filter or downstream structured-output verification that alters request execution beyond standard runtime behavior.
- Duration: up to 14 consecutive days unless both parties agree to extension.
- Scope: applies only when DeltaStack enables the agreed telemetry flag and remains within the agreed rate cap.
- Credits: If the issue persists beyond the carve-out without remediation, standard SLA credits apply retroactively for the breach period beyond the carve-out window.

Next steps: if this wording looks OK, Legal will prepare an amendment. I included a HubSpot link to the deal for tracking.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — the draft looks reasonable. We agree to the telemetry hook and rate cap. A couple of asks from Procurement:
- Please note that if the same failure pattern continues beyond the two-week window we will expect a proportional service credit for impaired availability during the extended period.
- Can we get access to the telemetry dashboard or a daily digest while this is active? Jacob (cc) will coordinate the technical hookup.

Emily will be the procurement owner for signatures. Once Legal sends the amendment we'll route it internally.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Rohit

Date: 2026-10-28T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Final: approval of timeboxed carve-out (conditions & next steps)

Rohit / team —

We can approve a 14-day, timeboxed carve-out for "filter-induced tool-call latency" under the conditions Karthik outlined and Ben captured in the draft language. Conditions summary:
- DeltaStack enables the telemetry flag and grants read access to the agreed dashboard feed (or receives a daily digest).
- Rate cap applied: max 20% of volume or 500 RPS (whichever lower).
- Automatic monitoring: if latency or error thresholds breach the defined rollback thresholds, the carve-out auto-revokes and standard SLAs apply.
- If the issue continues past 14 days, credits apply retroactively for the period past the window.

Next steps: legal will prepare the amendment (Ben, please loop Legal). Jacob — let's coordinate the telemetry hookup; Jasmine and Karthik will provide the config for the async pass-through and model-variant fallback. I'll schedule a weekly 30-min sync starting Monday to monitor.

Thanks everyone — let's keep the scope tight so we can get DeltaStack renewed without blocking procurement.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
